message:
Aero-Rotor Lead:

For Power-Systems Engineer and the Manager, the lower winding still lets the same blades do the same work, only volts rise into range. Plain words: the rotor still spins at the same speeds and makes the same shaft push, the generator just turns it into higher volts. Speeds stay 1.43e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) to 3.15e+03 RPM in the rpm at 11 m/s (E13) with shaft 3.27 W in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11), while revised volts 8.41 V low to 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) sit inside the window I take up from the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which needs 8 V minimum to make regulated 12 V, where Kv, meaning turns per volt, is 170 to 180. Starting twist 0.022 N·m in the operating torques (E73) still beats cogging of order 0.01 N·m, like a firm finger twist beating light stickiness, so start at 5 m/s stays.

For Safety-Control Integrator, soft stall plus three-blade solidity keeps your spring hold in charge at storm and lets the stop stay quick. Plain words: stalled blades only shiver while the bigger spring grips harder, and tip speed stays well below anything loud or strange. Tip 66.0 m/s in the tip speed check (E72) is highway-car speed not aircraft speed, so noise and vibration stay ordinary, and my stalled estimate about 0.25 N·m stays below your 0.80 N·m hold in the upgraded stop (E70), which I check as a hand grip beating a shopping-bag pull; I confirm what you take from the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that brakes are spring-applied fail-safe, which from rotor side means Tip-Speed Ratio (TSR), meaning tip speed over wind speed, 6 can run away electrically so friction must do the parking.

Ready, because v2 with 170 to 180 Kv keeps rotor power and speeds with volts inside regulation and hold over storm torque, and my remaining power-curve and parked-torque checks are named bench tests.
